tasks.title: Package the dashboard as an Electron app with electron-updater and a signed update channel
tasks.instructions: Electron with electron-builder and electron-updater, reused from Case Forge. Generic provider pointed at https://updates.clawdie.ai (proposed) serving per-platform latest.yml. Code-signing and updater keys only in GitHub secrets. Builds for macOS (arm64+x64), Windows, Linux. Session token via Electron safeStorage. Desktop path decided in COLLAB-20260921-08 (supersedes the cloudflared-token item in AUTH-DESIGN G1 item 5): the Electron shell loads the deployed web app from the approved HTTPS origin in a hardened BrowserWindow with a persistent partition. Access login, Turnstile, the __Host- cookie, CSRF and Origin then behave exactly as in a browser; no service credential, token store or PKCE flow ships in the installer. Hardening: contextIsolation on, sandbox on, nodeIntegration off, no preload API beyond the updater and window controls, will-navigate and setWindowOpenHandler limited to the app origin, the Access team domain and GitHub's login pages, all permission requests denied, external links opened in the system browser. The shell adds window chrome, the Downloads tab, notifications and an offline notice. Updates: electron-updater generic provider on the updates hostname with explicit user acceptance before install; unsigned dev builds labelled until signing is decided (T-020); rollback keeps the previous installer and the feed can pin or withdraw a version; revocation of an old shell via a minimum-version field on /config answered with 426. Cookie bridge (COLLAB-20260921-09): the updater's own net session gets only the current CF_Authorization and __Host-platform-session cookies, read from the app partition at request time (never cached or logged), attached only to requests whose URL is exactly the app origin plus the feed path prefix, with redirects cancelled before any cookie is attached; latest.yml must carry relative file names only. Update checks run only after the renderer has confirmed a live session (GET /me 200) and never loop on a failed feed (Access renewal is done in the window, not by the updater). Per-user NSIS install without elevation. Electron 44.2.0, electron-builder 26.15.3, electron-updater 6.8.9 pinned.

tasks.title: Release pipeline: tag -> installers -> R2 -> download link posted to the board
tasks.instructions: On a v* tag: build all installers, upload to Cloudflare R2 (public bucket behind updates.clawdie.ai), write the latest.yml manifests for electron-updater, create a GitHub Release, append a note to board/notes.md with the download links, message the Claude session over MCP, and populate the Downloads tab from the same manifests. This mirrors Case Forge's update-link flow. M5 feed decisions (COLLAB-20260921-09): the Windows x64 feed is served same-origin by the Worker at /api/updates/windows/x64/ (latest.yml and installer bytes streamed from private R2, Cache-Control: no-store, GET only, session and terms required, no CSRF for GET), so Access and the host-only app cookie protect it without a second hostname; an updates hostname is deferred until DeAndre answers. latest.yml is unsigned in electron-updater 6, so integrity rests on TLS plus Access, the sha512 in the manifest, a strict Authenticode check (Valid trust, timestamp, pinned publisher subject, an allowlist of certificate thumbprints holding the current and the next certificate so renewal never strands installed clients) run at download and again immediately before install because a cache hit skips the download callback, and a monotonic version rule (never equal or lower). Consequence: rollback is forward-only: withdraw the bad version from the feed and publish a rebuilt earlier version under a higher version number. Minimum-version on /config is a compatibility gate answered with 426, never a revocation; revocation stays in Worker session policy.

tasks.title: M1: Worker + D1 accounts (invite, signup, verification, login, reset, roles, avatar, terms) behind Access
tasks.instructions: Implement the M1 design note (T-018) after Fable's review. Endpoints under the names in docs/API.md section 5-6. Acceptance tests from docs/prompts/astra-platform-brief.md section 6 (auth, roles, avatar, terms). Secrets only in Cloudflare secrets. PR into main (or baseline) from codex/platform-app; Fable reviews the auth and session code before merge. G1 fixes (COLLAB-20260921-03), all required before merge: (1) Hashing: @noble/hashes 2.4.0 PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 at 600000 iterations is approved; add known-answer tests (RFC 6070 vectors plus at least three salt/length cases) run in CI, verify the package integrity hash against the npm registry tarball at install, and cap the Worker at one KDF call per request. (2) Request order on login/signup/forgot/reset: exact Origin and JSON content type and body-size check, then limiter reservation in the auth Durable Object (per-IP and per-account, before anything external), then Turnstile siteverify, then account lookup, then the single KDF call. Failed attempts count; a success resets the per-account window; add a global ceiling of 60 KDF calls per minute across the Worker so an attacker cannot buy CPU time with valid Turnstile tokens; a locked account still allows the reset flow under its own limiter, so the owner cannot be locked out of recovery. (3) Identity binding: invitation email and Access email may differ. Bind on first successful invite-token redemption: the token proves the invited address, the validated Access JWT proves the identity; store Access sub as the primary binding and the Access email as informational; refuse redemption if that sub is already bound to another user; later logins require the same sub; an email change on the same sub is allowed and audited; a sub change requires the owner to re-bind. (4) Access JWT: jose with alg allowlist RS256 only, exact iss and aud, JWKS cached with bounded TTL, fail closed. (5) Desktop: after the browser login and PKCE code exchange, Electron must also hold the Access token for the API hostname (sent as the Cf-Access-Jwt-Assertion header) or the Access app for the API hostname must carry a longer session than the web app; decide and record which, since the app session alone does not pass the Access perimeter. (6) SameSite=Strict on the session cookie is fine because verify and reset are token-only routes that need no session; state that in the design so nobody relaxes it later. (7) Avatar decode: name the decoder (Cloudflare Images binding or a pinned WASM decoder) before implementation; uploads stay disabled until it is chosen.

(F2, before staging) reserve() runs before verifyAccess() on password routes, so a request with an expired or invalid Access assertion consumes the named account's window and, for login, counts toward the ten-failure lock; verify the assertion first (JWKS is cached), then reserve. tasks.title: Production hosting integration: Workers Static Assets wrapper, worker-first routing, Access before assets, private deploy config (review gate G4)
tasks.instructions: Deliver a code head for review. G4 checklist, all required before the first deploy: (1) /api/* is the only API prefix in production; drop the unprefixed route alias so asset paths and API routes cannot collide. (2) run_worker_first covers every path, so no asset is served before the Worker verifies the Access assertion; non-API requests are GET/HEAD only, then verifyAccess, then ASSETS.fetch; a request without the assertion gets 403, not the page. (3) Security headers on asset responses are set by the wrapper, not only by _headers; not_found_handling is not the SPA fallback, so unknown paths return 404. (4) workers_dev and preview_urls stay false; only the custom domain app.clawdie.ai is routed; confirm the custom domain adds one DNS record and touches nothing at the apex or inbox. (5) Access application per T-024; Turnstile widget for the exact hostname; secrets only via wrangler secret put. (6) EMAIL_FROM on a sender domain whose SPF/DKIM already accommodate Cloudflare sending; the apex SPF record is a Microsoft mail setting and stays human-controlled; one test send to the owner before any verification mail. (7) D1 created and 0001 applied once; only the database name goes on the board; export before any later migration. (8) First deploy with AVATAR_READY, EVENTS_READY, DOWNLOADS_READY, board binding and RUN_ORIGIN unset. (9) No installer in the release bucket and updatesEnabled false until the signing decision; the strict verifier cannot install an unsigned build. (10) Decide observability: enabled with sampling is recommended since tokens never appear in URLs. (11) wrangler deploy --dry-run first; deploy from the reviewed commit; record commit and Worker version id; rollback is wrangler rollback plus forward-compatible D1. (12) Smoke before any invite: unauthenticated GET / redirects to Access at the edge; authenticated GET / carries CSP and no-store; GET /api/config 200 with all features false; GET /api/me 401; POST without Origin 403; /api/events 503; GET /nope 404.
